focalEvent.label: Instrument-air low-pressure indication at RHOB receiving header P-R triggered alarm AL-44 and paused work.
focalEvent.detail: At approximately 10:00 AM on May 20, 2024, the RHOB process area reported loss of instrument-air pressure while a two-person Utilities team was preparing the #1 slab caster (1SC) compressor/dryer system for planned maintenance. The work was paused and the air supply was subsequently restored.

nodes.label: Utilities air gallery serves RHOB process area; local indication P-R normally shows normal pressure band.
nodes.detail: The Utilities air gallery distributes instrument air to the RHOB process area. The receiving header H-R at RHOB has a local indication point P-R that typically displays within a normal operating range (above 5.0 bar).

nodes.label: Alarm AL-44 activates when P-R pressure drops below 4.5 bar and clears above 5.0 bar.
nodes.detail: The RHOB PLC low-pressure input from point P-R (AL-44) is configured to trigger a 'COMP FAULT' indication if the measured pressure falls below 4.5 bar, and it resets when pressure rises above 5.0 bar.

nodes.label: At 10:00 AM, P-R pressure dropped from ~6.8 bar to below alarm thresholds (<4.5 bar).
nodes.detail: RHOB operations detected an instrument-air low-pressure indication at the receiving header (P-R), dropping from approximately 6.8 bar to a value that triggered the AL-44 alarm.

nodes.detail: Upon receiving notification of the low-pressure indication, Utilities operations formally acknowledged the issue around 10:02 AM and immediately halted all maintenance activities pending further review.

The incident description notes that work had been paused earlier but does not specify whether full restoration of service or just a temporary pressure recovery occurred before maintenance was deferred until later (by 10:20).

decision.summary: The board currently explains the event as a low-pressure indication at P-R that triggered AL-44 and paused work, but it does not yet explain why pressure dropped. The causal chain is incomplete because we lack evidence of what physically interrupted flow or caused the alarm condition.
unknowns: The exact point of interruption in the distribution system.
Whether a valve was inadvertently opened or closed during boundary preparation.
alternatives: A compressor trip caused loss of supply to all downstream headers including P-R.
An isolated maintenance action on another line affected shared piping upstream of RHOB.
The crew may have misinterpreted a normal transient fluctuation as an alarm condition.

edges.rationale: The pressure drop at P-R (condition n-ax2alr) directly triggered the alarm AL-44 and work pause defined in focal. The point register shows a continuous decline from 6.8 bar to below thresholds, crossing the activation limit of 4.5 bar.
edges.counterfactual: If P-R pressure had remained above 4.5 bar at 10:00, AL-44 would not have activated and work would not have paused.
edges.competingExplanation: None; the alarm logic is deterministic based on input value.
edges.evidenceGap: The exact mechanism of the pressure drop (source vs downstream) remains unknown.

edges.rationale: Normal operation at P-R established a baseline where any drop below 4.5 bar would be detected by AL-44.
edges.counterfactual: If P-R were normally below 5.0 bar, the alarm might have been masked or ignored.
edges.competingExplanation: None; normal operation is a prerequisite for detecting an anomaly.
edges.evidenceGap: The specific threshold values are known from point register.

edges.rationale: Alarm AL-44 activates below 4.5 bar and clears above 5.0 bar, providing the detection mechanism for the pressure drop.
edges.counterfactual: If the alarm threshold were higher or lower, detection timing would differ.
edges.competingExplanation: None; this is a system design fact.
edges.evidenceGap: The mapping of AL-44 to P-R input is confirmed by point register.

edges.rationale: Blank work package field execution record indicates incomplete boundary preparation, which may have contributed to the team's vulnerability when air was lost.
edges.counterfactual: If the work package had been fully executed and signed, boundary conditions might have mitigated impact.
edges.competingExplanation: The blank field alone does not prove a procedural failure; it may reflect timing of record entry vs. alarm occurrence.
edges.evidenceGap: Whether the blank field represented an actual omission or simply delayed documentation is unknown.

edges.rationale: Pending maintenance acceptance signature suggests the boundary was not formally released, potentially leaving equipment in an unverified state.
edges.counterfactual: If acceptance had been signed, the boundary would have been formally released and equipment verified.
edges.competingExplanation: Pending signature may reflect administrative timing rather than operational status; no evidence of unsafe condition is provided.
edges.evidenceGap: Whether pending signature correlated with an unverified valve state or other hazard remains unknown.

edges.rationale: Unknown whether crew saw recent changes; if they did not, this could have contributed to misinterpretation of equipment state.

nodes.label: A command, a field-position observation and a proved internal valve condition are different records.
nodes.detail: IA-D02 distinguishes these record types. The incident evidence contains commands (requests for attendance) but lacks direct observations of valve states or proven conditions at the time of failure.

nodes.label: The 1SC gallery and RHOB instrument-air station are separate operating locations.
nodes.detail: IA-D01 defines these as distinct. This implies the air loss could originate in either location or at their interface, complicating origin identification without additional data.

nodes.label: Maintenance receives the work boundary only after its release.
nodes.detail: IA-D01 states that Utilities prepares the maintenance boundary, and Maintenance (M-A) accepts it later. At 10:00 AM, M-A's signature was not yet obtained per IA-S02, suggesting incomplete handover of control or information.

nodes.label: Utilities air gallery serves RHOB process area and distributes instrument air to the receiving header H-R.
nodes.detail: The directory identifies RHOB as a local area name for records, not an individual compressor. The gallery supplies 1SC dryer group D-101 and routes air to RHOB.

nodes.label: Local indication P-R at RHOB receiving header H-R normally shows normal pressure band.
nodes.detail: The point register maps AL-44 to the receiving-header pressure condition. Normal operation implies a 'normal band' reading before 10:00 AM (6.8 bar).

nodes.label: Pressure upstream of distribution routes (P-U) remained stable at 6.9 bar during the event window.
nodes.detail: Measurements show P-U was constant at 6.8–6.9 bar from 09:54 to 10:08, indicating supply pressure did not drop significantly upstream of RHOB.

nodes.label: Maintenance acceptance signature was not yet signed at notification time.
nodes.detail: The work package cover explicitly states 'Maintenance acceptance signature: not yet signed' when the incident occurred, meaning formal boundary release had not been granted.

nodes.label: No line opening was authorized at the time of interruption.
nodes.detail: Shift log entry at 10:02 AM explicitly records 'No line opening authorized' while work was paused and issue under review.

nodes.label: Area directory does not establish valve positions or pressure availability at any given time.
nodes.detail: The area and service directory is a location index only; it explicitly states it 'does not establish valve positions or the pressure available at any given time.'

nodes.label: Desk entries do not log every field operation or identify the point of interruption.
nodes.detail: The shift log excerpt states 'desk entries do not log every field operation' and explicitly notes they 'do not identify the point at which the air supply was interrupted.'

nodes.label: No documented confirmation of understanding regarding root cause assessment or response steps is present.
nodes.detail: Evidence shows no interview concerning fatigue, workload, intent, or discussion confirming how the interruption was handled beyond pausing work.

nodes.label: RHOB reported an 'air-low' indication and requested Utilities attendance at ~10:00 AM.
nodes.detail: Shift log records RHOB entry stating 'Air-low indication. Local controls showing supply complaints. Requested Utilities attendance.'

nodes.label: Utilities acknowledged receipt of the issue at ~10:02 AM and paused work.
nodes.detail: Shift log records Utilities entry stating 'Work paused. RHOB service issue under review.' following RHOB's request for attendance.

nodes.label: Local indication P-R dropped from 6.8 bar to below alarm threshold (5.0 bar) between 10:00 and 10:03 AM.
nodes.detail: Pressure samples show P-R at 6.8 bar at 09:54, dropping to 5.8 bar at 10:00:11, then 4.1 bar at 10:00:40 (below AL-44 alarm threshold of 4.5 bar).

nodes.label: Alarm AL-44 triggered at 10:00:32 and was acknowledged by Utilities.
nodes.detail: Pressure samples show P-R below alarm threshold starting at 10:00:11. Alarm journal shows occurrence time of 10:00:32, acknowledgment at 10:03:14.

nodes.label: Normal pressure returned at ~10:07 AM after alarm cleared.
nodes.detail: Pressure samples show P-R returning to 6.0 bar by 10:06:20 and normal band (6.8 bar) by 10:06:50. RHOB requested retention of records at this time.

nodes.label: Crew U-A/U-B had current Utilities operating qualification and energy-control authorization.
nodes.detail: Assignment extract lists both operators with 'Current Utilities operating qualification and energy-control authorization' at shift start.

nodes.label: Maintenance receiver M-A had boundary acceptance pending.
nodes.detail: Assignment extract lists M-A with 'boundary acceptance pending' status at shift start, consistent with work package cover noting signature not yet signed.

nodes.label: Work folder WO-527-E was blank at issue time.
nodes.detail: Work package cover attachment index shows 'WO-527-E: Blank at folder issue' for the field execution record, indicating no pre-filled isolation steps or valve states were documented on handover.

nodes.label: Daily work briefing topic line read '1SC dryer work and RHOB service coordination'.
nodes.detail: Assignment extract notes the daily briefing attendance sheet contains no valve-by-valve content, only a general topic line.

edges.rationale: Normal operation at P-R established a baseline where any drop below 4.5 bar would be detected by AL-44.

rejectedEdges.toLabel: Utilities air gallery serves RHOB process area; local indication P-R normally shows normal pressure band.

The evidence supports both nodes independently.
proposal.counterfactual: If the air gallery did not serve RHOB, a drop at P-R would not be described as an 'RHOB receiving header' event.

proposal.evidenceGap: No gap.

questions.text: What specific equipment failure, valve mispositioning, or upstream disturbance interrupted instrument-air flow into receiving header H-R? Is there a record of compressor trip, dryer malfunction, line rupture, or unauthorized isolation?
questions.intent: Identify the physical mechanism that caused P-R pressure to drop below 4.5 bar at 10:00 AM.
questions.rationale: The evidence confirms the pressure drop and alarm but does not identify whether it originated at the source (compressor/dryer), within distribution piping, or due to an isolated valve action. Determining this is essential for constructing a causal chain.

questions.text: Request engineering drawings and work orders for instrument-air distribution between March 1 and May 20, 2024. Verify if any changes to valves M-101/M-102 or routing affecting RHOB were documented and approved per IA-D03 Section 3.6.
questions.intent: Determine whether an unapproved service-routing change or undocumented valve closure caused the P-R pressure drop.
questions.rationale: If an unrecorded change exists, it would explain the localized P-R drop while upstream pressure remained stable. Absence of such a record does not prove absence of action; requires direct evidence.
evidenceNeeded: Engineering disposition records for instrument-air routing changes
Valve status logs or field reports from 09:54–10:08

questions.text: Request field notes, checklists, or interview transcripts from U-A/U-B regarding pre-work verification of P-R pressure and relevant valve positions at 09:48–10:00 AM.
questions.intent: Verify whether the Utilities crew performed a valve-status confirmation before starting boundary preparation.
questions.rationale: If the crew did not confirm current system state before starting work, this could constitute a procedural gap contributing to vulnerability when an unexpected disturbance occurred.

questions.text: Request operator logs or interview excerpts describing actions taken immediately after AL-44 triggered (e.g., checking compressor status vs. investigating supply-side pressure loss).
questions.intent: Assess whether the alarm label 'COMP FAULT' delayed troubleshooting by misdirecting initial response.
questions.rationale: If operators assumed a mechanical fault due to the label, this could have delayed identification of the true cause (supply interruption).

questions.text: What physical mechanism (e.g., valve failure, upstream supply loss, sensor malfunction) triggered the pressure drop observed between 10:00 and 10:06 AM?
questions.intent: Identify the specific equipment or process condition that caused the air-low indication at RHOB P-R.
questions.rationale: Evidence explicitly states origin unknown. Identifying cause requires examining distribution system logs, maintenance records for recent changes, or operator observations not captured in current packet.
evidenceNeeded: Upstream supply pressure record (P-U) with higher sampling frequency
Maintenance work orders executed near 1SC compressor/dryer system prior to incident

questions.text: Did the pressure loss affect only RHOB P-R or also impact upstream/downstream locations like North gallery (P-U)?
questions.intent: Determine whether simultaneous low-pressure events occurred at other downstream points such as North gallery.
questions.rationale: Current evidence shows sampling limitations prevent confirmation of simultaneous events elsewhere. Establishing scope requires additional data from other monitoring points.
evidenceNeeded: Pressure extract including North gallery/P-U continuous waveform or higher-frequency samples during incident window

questions.text: Was an approved temporary instruction or revised energy-control procedure (ECP) issued for the 1SC dryer maintenance boundary before the air-low event?
questions.intent: Verify whether a temporary instruction was attached to work package WO-527 prior to incident.
questions.rationale: Work package cover shows blank attachment field. Requires checking change records, engineering dispositions, and distribution logs to confirm if ECP revision existed.
evidenceNeeded: Change record IA-D03 showing issued temporary instruction or revised ECP for WO-527
Engineering disposition document authorizing changed arrangement

questions.text: Was there a recorded agreement or briefing confirming both teams understood the meaning of AL-44 'COMP FAULT' display text before incident?
questions.intent: Confirm whether documented confirmation existed between Utilities and RHOB regarding air-low alarm understanding.
questions.rationale: Shift log shows request for attendance but no explicit record of shared understanding. Requires reviewing coordination logs, training records, or interview summaries.
evidenceNeeded: Training extract showing AL-44 alarm interpretation instruction

questions.text: What physical mechanism (e.g., stuck-open valve, ruptured line, faulty regulator) caused the pressure loss between ~10:00 AM and 10:03 AM? Which drawing, inspection record, or maintenance history could confirm this?
questions.intent: Identify the specific valve or component that failed and caused the localized pressure drop at P-R.
questions.rationale: Without knowing the exact failure point, corrective actions may target the wrong system component. Evidence gaps include lack of valve state logs, flow data, or physical damage reports.
evidenceNeeded: Valve position records for RHOB distribution path
Maintenance history for P-R sensor/regulator assembly

questions.text: Did the absence of a completed field execution record (WO-527-E) mean that required valve closures or checks were not performed? What procedure mandates completion before work begins?
questions.intent: Determine whether the blank WO-527-E field execution record contributed to the event by omitting critical isolation steps.
questions.rationale: If procedural non-compliance is confirmed, it becomes a root cause candidate. However, we must first establish whether any documented requirement explicitly demanded this field be filled prior to starting.
evidenceNeeded: Procedure requiring completion of execution record before work start

questions.text: Was formal boundary release required by procedure before starting work? If so, did U-A/U-B proceed without it?
questions.intent: Clarify whether the unsigned maintenance acceptance signature indicates incomplete boundary release.
questions.rationale: Unsigned signatures may indicate procedural gaps but do not automatically prove unauthorized action unless a requirement exists and was violated. Need to verify if 'maintenance released' status is mandatory.

questions.text: How did RHOB notify Utilities of the air-low condition? Was there a standard protocol for such notifications, and was it followed?
questions.intent: Assess whether communication gaps contributed to delayed response or miscoordination.
questions.rationale: Unclear communication channels could delay recognition or escalation. Need evidence on notification methods (radio vs phone) and response SLAs.
evidenceNeeded: Standard operating procedure for alarm reporting

questions.text: Did U-A/U-B review any revised drawings, P&IDs, or change notices before starting work? Is there evidence of a briefing session?
questions.intent: Verify whether the crew received recent training or briefings on updated system configurations.
questions.rationale: Lack of awareness about new equipment states could lead to unexpected interactions. Need confirmation of training records or sign-offs.

questions.text: Why was the AL-44 label not updated after equipment changes? Does this mislabeling affect operator response or troubleshooting?
questions.intent: Understand why the alarm display retained legacy text ('COMP FAULT') despite mapping to pressure input.
questions.rationale: Legacy labels can confuse operators during emergencies. Need engineering change order records and UI update logs.
evidenceNeeded: Engineering change orders for alarm screen

questions.text: Were there known high-noise zones or long distances between RHOB and Utilities control rooms that could degrade message clarity?
questions.intent: Determine if environmental factors (noise, distance) impacted communication reliability.
questions.rationale: Environmental conditions might explain missed alarms or delayed acknowledgments. Need site layout maps and noise level data.

questions.text: Was there an engineering disposition or approved temporary instruction attached to ECP-1SC-04 prior to WO-527 issuance, specifically addressing any changes affecting RHOB service routing?
questions.intent: Determine if a service-routing change occurred that affected the maintenance boundary for RHOB instrument-air between March and May 2024.
questions.rationale: If yes: The blank attachment field may indicate a procedural gap in documenting the change. If no: The interruption might stem from an unrelated upstream/downstream event not captured by current evidence.

questions.text: Request the full ECP revision history for instrument-air distribution to RHOB (ECP-1SC-04) from March through May 2024, including any redlines or engineering disposition records. Also request maintenance logs showing valve operations in the Utilities air gallery during this period.
questions.intent: Determine whether an unrecorded service-routing change or valve state alteration occurred between March and May 2024 affecting RHOB.
questions.rationale: If an unrecorded change occurred and was not revised/attached per IA-D03 requirements, it would explain why a blank temporary instruction field existed while supply conditions changed unexpectedly.
evidenceNeeded: Maintenance logs showing valve operations in Utilities air gallery

questions.text: Request alarm history and PLC input logs for AL-44 at RHOB from 10:00 AM on May 20, including any associated valve position indicators (if available). Also request utility outage reports or maintenance work orders affecting the instrument-air header upstream of H-R during Turn 2.
questions.intent: Determine whether the point register (IA-P02) or other records can identify if P-R pressure dropped due to upstream isolation vs source failure.
questions.rationale: Distinguishing between a distribution system isolation and source failure is critical for determining whether this was an equipment malfunction vs procedural gap. Valve state records would confirm if barriers were properly maintained.
evidenceNeeded: Utility outage reports or upstream maintenance work orders

questions.text: Request interview notes or shift supervisor statements from Utilities operations regarding any known service-routing changes affecting RHOB between March and May 2024. Also request coordination logs showing communication about potential supply disruptions during Turn 2 maintenance preparations.
questions.intent: Determine whether the blank temporary instruction field was intentional (no change) vs an oversight due to unrecorded changes.
questions.rationale: If no change occurred, the blank field is a documentation gap but not necessarily a causal factor. If an unrecorded change existed, it would be a procedural failure per IA-D03 requirements.
evidenceNeeded: Coordination logs for Turn 2 maintenance preparations

questions.text: Request shift logs and alarm records from other areas served by the same instrument-air header (e.g., 1SC gallery, North gallery) for May 20 around 10:00 AM. Also request any cross-functional notifications about utility outages or maintenance activities affecting shared infrastructure.
questions.intent: Determine whether the air-low indication at RHOB was isolated to this area or part of a broader supply disturbance.
questions.rationale: If only RHOB was affected, it suggests a localized issue (valve position, local isolation). If multiple areas were affected, it points to upstream source failure.
evidenceNeeded: Shift logs and alarm records from other served areas

questions.text: Request training records and recent change briefings for U-A/U-B regarding instrument-air system configurations, especially any updates since March 2024. Also request daily briefing content from May 20 showing whether valve-by-valve status was communicated (if required by procedure).
questions.intent: Determine whether the crew's lack of awareness about potential supply changes contributed to their inability to respond effectively.
questions.rationale: If the crew lacked awareness of recent changes or proper procedures for verifying supply conditions before work release, this would be a contributing factor.
evidenceNeeded: Training records and change briefings for U-A/U-B

questions.text: Request maintenance release documentation for WO-527, including any pre-release checks performed by Utilities operations. Also request records showing who authorized the crew to proceed with boundary preparation and what information they received about current valve states or known issues.
questions.intent: Determine whether the work boundary acceptance process was followed correctly given potential supply changes.
questions.rationale: If proper verification of supply conditions was not required before work release (or if it was but not done), this would be a procedural failure.

questions.text: Request latest piping diagrams and valve position records for the instrument-air distribution system serving RHOB. Compare these with the IA-P02 point register to identify any discrepancies between documented signals and actual physical conditions.
questions.intent: Determine whether the point register mapping (IA-P02) accurately reflects current system configuration.
questions.rationale: If the point register is outdated or misconfigured, it could mask real supply issues until they manifest as alarms.
evidenceNeeded: Latest piping diagrams for instrument-air distribution

questions.text: Request maintenance logs for P-R pressure transmitter and AL-44 input module from May 20. Also request any calibration records or fault history for these devices.
questions.intent: Determine whether the air-low indication was a false alarm due to sensor or PLC configuration issues.
questions.rationale: If this was a false alarm, the root cause would be equipment failure rather than procedural gaps.
evidenceNeeded: Maintenance logs for P-R pressure transmitter
Calibration and fault history for AL-44

questions.text: Request the completed WO-527-E field execution record to verify boundary verification steps performed by U-A/U-B. Does this document show valve states, isolation confirmations, or acceptance signatures prior to 10:00 AM?
questions.intent: Determine whether the blank field execution record (WO-527-E) was filled before or after the air interruption, and what data it contained if any.
questions.rationale: A filled record would establish whether procedural controls were executed; a blank one suggests missing documentation but not necessarily physical failure.

questions.text: Request pressure trend logs from P-U and P-R points between 09:35 and 10:20 to locate where pressure dropped first. Does a drop at P-U indicate upstream source failure; simultaneous drops suggest distribution issue?
questions.intent: Identify the physical point of air interruption (source, distribution network, or receiving equipment).
questions.rationale: Point register maps AL-44 to receiving header but does not show full network behavior; trend data could distinguish location of fault.

questions.text: Request any change orders or routing-change notices effective between 2024-03-01 (IA-D03 effective date) and May 20, 2024. Does Engineering have approved a revised ECP for the RHOB/1SC boundary?
questions.intent: Verify whether a recent service-routing change affected the maintenance boundary and if engineering disposition was completed.
questions.rationale: Change records could explain why crew used outdated drawings or missed new isolation points; absence of disposition supports procedural gap hypothesis.

questions.text: Request training attendance logs or interview notes indicating if crew reviewed DW-1SC-17 Revision A and any associated change briefings before 09:35 AM.
questions.intent: Confirm whether U-A/U-B received a recent change briefing for the equipment-location sheet (DW-1SC-17).
questions.rationale: If no briefing occurred, crew may have relied on outdated drawings; this supports a procedural gap but does not prove physical cause of air loss.

questions.text: Request work package issue logs to see who prepared IA-S02 and whether a temporary instruction should have been attached per change requirements (IA-D03 Section 3.6).
questions.intent: Determine if the blank temporary instruction attachment field was intentional or an oversight.
questions.rationale: If omission was unintentional, it points to administrative error; if intentional without approval, suggests procedural bypass.

questions.text: What specific valve, line break, or upstream disturbance caused the instrument air pressure to drop from normal (6.8 bar) to low (<4.5 bar) in the RHOB receiving header between 10:00 and 10:03 AM?
questions.intent: Identify the physical mechanism causing P-R pressure drop at RHOB.
questions.rationale: The evidence shows P-U remained stable while P-R dropped, suggesting a localized issue downstream of P-U or within the distribution path to RHOB. Without knowing the mechanism (e.g., closed valve, leak, compressor trip), we cannot determine if it was an equipment failure, procedural error, or external event.

questions.text: Was the pressure drop caused by a failure in the 1SC compressor/dryer system (upstream) or by an issue specific to the line serving RHOB?
questions.intent: Determine if the interruption occurred upstream of RHOB's receiving header or within its local distribution.
questions.rationale: The incident description states 'initial notification does not establish whether the interruption began at the air source, within the distribution system, or at the receiving equipment.' Clarifying this location is essential for root cause analysis.

questions.text: Were there documented steps taken to isolate affected equipment or secure boundaries when work was paused at 10:02 AM?
questions.intent: Verify if any isolation or boundary procedures were followed during the interruption event.
questions.rationale: The evidence shows 'No line opening authorized' but does not confirm whether standard emergency response protocols (e.g., isolating valves, tagging out) were executed. This affects recurrence prevention.

questions.text: Was the alarm AL-44 ('COMP FAULT') properly mapped to monitor receiving-header pressure (P-R) rather than an unrelated signal like C-11 RUN?

questions.rationale: The point register states 'PR-12 maps it [AL-44] to the receiving-header pressure condition, not to C-11's trip contact,' but this is a synthetic record. Verification ensures alarms accurately reflect actual conditions.

questions.text: Did the absence of pre-filled valve states or isolation steps in WO-527-E lead to miscommunication between RHOB and Utilities?

questions.text: Request the latest configuration drawing revision and any field-change logs for the instrument-air distribution system covering May 20, 2024. Specifically ask: Was there a documented routing change affecting RHOB receiving header H-R between shift start (07:00) and air loss (~10:00)? If yes, was it communicated to Utilities operations or included in the daily briefing?
questions.intent: Determine whether an unrecorded service-routing change or undocumented valve state actually occurred at the time of the incident.
questions.rationale: If an unrecorded change occurred, correcting record-keeping procedures could prevent recurrence. Absence of evidence currently leaves this as unknown; obtaining drawings/logs would resolve whether a physical mechanism (routing change) caused the loss.

Field-change logs or work orders documenting valve states between 07:00 and 10:00 on May 20, 2024
